title: Current and Horizon
premise: Odile Okafor, estranged child of a disgraced archaeologist and a better digger than their father ever was, is drowning in his debts when a freak low tide uncovers a sea cave on a leased concession — and inside it, a bronze mechanism that rewrites the region's history. A well-funded rival expedition and the concession's corrupt backer both want the find, and Odile must smuggle the discovery home with a ragtag crew before the permits expire, choosing between selling the truth and protecting the crew that has become their first real family. In the end, Odile floods the cave rather than surrender it, publishes nothing, and finds that belonging was the treasure the legends were charging admission to all along.
about_author: B. M. Blackwood is the pen name of a former maritime surveyor who spent a decade charting coastlines before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people who find themselves in the last places anyone looks.

chapters.title: The Tide's Ledger
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Broke and hounded by creditors, Odile takes a salvage contract on the concession their father once disgraced himself over. A record low tide exposes a cave mouth sealed since antiquity, and Odile — against every instinct — steps inside, finding carved bronze that shouldn't exist. The beat is reluctant hope: the debt might finally have an exit, if the cave doesn't kill them first.

chapters.title: Concession
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, with interludes from crew engineer Tomas. Odile assembles a skeleton crew under cover of routine survey work, but the concession's backer, Veyra, smells the find and tightens her grip — permits, pay, and a veiled threat. Odile lies to the crew about what they're really doing, and the lie curdles. The beat is rising dread: duty to the debt pulling against the first loyalty Odile has felt in years.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Veyra's men storm the site; in the scramble, the cave's flooded inner chamber is breached and the mechanism begins to corrode in open air. Odile must confess the truth to the crew — and Tomas, betrayed but unwilling to walk away, helps them rig a salvage that will destroy the find rather than surrender it. The beat is the climax: love and belonging declared in the act of choosing each other over the discovery, the debt, and Veyra.

chapters.title: Horizon Line
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. With the permits expiring at dawn, the crew floods the cave and holds Veyra's salvage barge off with nothing but paperwork and nerve. Odile settles the debt honestly, publishes a deliberately dull geological report, and watches the sea close over the site. The beat is quiet resolution: power refused, family kept, and a horizon that finally belongs to them.
